title: Support for delivery riders after a food delivery platform exits Singapore
asked: Ms Yeo Wan Ling asked what protections are in place for workers affected by a food delivery platform company exiting Singapore, whether platform companies must provide notice and transition assistance, and whether additional measures will strengthen redeployment and income support during such disruptions.
response: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong said the question had been addressed by written reply to Question No 97 on 7 April 2026. In his supplementary reply, he said platform operators and platform work associations should continue bilateral discussions on information for workers, with NTUC having led discussions on industry-wide principles for payment and incentive structures announced on 11 September 2025. In the recent exit, the operator worked with Workforce Singapore, NTUC's Employment and Employability Institute, and unions to offer job matching, career coaching, outreach and transition. Workers can approach WSG for SkillsFuture and Career Conversion Programmes, and low-wage platform workers can seek financial assistance from social services offices.

key_points.point: The question was addressed by written reply to Question No 97 on 7 April 2026.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: this question for oral answer has been addressed by written reply, to Question No 97 on the Order Paper for the 7 April 2026 Sitting.

key_points.point: Platform operators and platform work associations should continue bilateral discussions on information provided to workers.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: platform operators and platform work associations should continue their bilateral discussions on the information that can be provided to workers.

key_points.point: NTUC led discussions with platform work associations and major platform operators to agree industry-wide principles on payment and incentive structures.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: NTUC has led many of these discussions, for example, with platform work associations, major platform operators, to agree on a set of industry-wide and accepted principles, in terms of payment and incentive structures.

key_points.point: Discussions covered fair earnings, visibility on structural changes and incentive schemes.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: Some of these things were discussed: for example, fair earnings, visibility on structural changes, incentive schemes.

key_points.point: These were announced on 11 September 2025 by NTUC.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: These were announced on 11 September 2025 by NTUC.

key_points.point: In this case, the food delivery operator worked with Workforce Singapore and NTUC's Employment and Employability Institute to offer job matching and career coaching.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: the food delivery operator, had really worked closely with Workforce Singapore (WSG) and also NTUC's Employment and Employability Institute to step in to offer job matching capabilities and also career coaching in times of need.

key_points.point: The operator also worked with the Singapore Manual and Mercantile Workers' Union and the National Delivery Champions Association to facilitate outreach and transition.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: The platform operator also worked, like what Member has mentioned, with the Singapore Manual and Mercantile Workers' Union and the National Delivery Champions Association to facilitate their outreach and transition.

key_points.point: Platform workers transitioning to full-time employment or a different platform can approach WSG for SkillsFuture and Career Conversion Programmes.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: they can always approach WSG with a suite of capabilities, SkillsFuture, as well as the Career Conversion Programmes.

key_points.point: Low-wage platform workers can approach the social services office for financial assistance.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: For low-wage platform workers, they can also approach the social services office to help with financial assistance.

left_open: Whether platform companies are required to provide notice and transition assistance.
Whether additional measures will be introduced to strengthen redeployment and income support during such disruptions.
Whether a more structured framework with coordinated support across agencies and industries is planned.
How workers are ensured against prolonged income disruption and hardship during the transition.
supplementary: The supplementary questions focused on clearer platform operator responsibilities on data transparency and worker communication, and a more structured cross-agency support framework for transitions.
